key_insight: Zero-shot compositional action models often rely on object-driven verb shortcuts—predicting verbs from object cues alone—because compositional supervision is extremely sparse and skewed and verbs are learned asymmetrically harder than objects. Mitigating these shortcuts via targeted rebalancing and compositional constraints substantially improves generalization to unseen verb–object pairs.
problem_solved: The paper addresses why ZS-CAR models fail to generalize to unseen verb–object combinations, identifying and fixing the hidden failure mode where objects dominate verb prediction (object-driven shortcuts).
method: Systematic diagnosis: quantify sparsity and skewness in compositional supervision and measure asymmetric learning of verbs vs. objects.

Mitigation suite: introduce training interventions (e.g., supervision rebalancing, compositional regularizers and contrastive objectives, and targeted data/augmentation strategies) that reduce object-driven shortcutting.
Evaluation: propose and use targeted metrics and splits to validate improved zero-shot compositional generalization and robustness.
impact: Provides practical interventions and diagnostics that make compositional action models more robust and better at generalizing to novel verb–object combinations—useful for researchers and practitioners building zero-shot action recognition systems from video.
visual_elements: Schematic showing object-driven shortcut: same object image with multiple ground-truth verbs but model predicting the same verb due to object bias.
Heatmap or bar chart of compositional supervision sparsity/skewness across verb-object pairs.
Before/after performance bars for zero-shot verb–object accuracy demonstrating the effect of mitigation strategies.
Pipeline diagram of proposed mitigation suite (diagnosis → rebalancing/regularization → evaluation).
paper_title: Why Can't I Open My Drawer? Mitigating Object-Driven Shortcuts in Zero-Shot Compositional Action Recognition
paper_authors: Geo Ahn, Inwoong Lee, Taeoh Kim, Minho Shim, Dongyoon Wee
